operator_io_quirks: Table 'RA' is mixed-case; must be double-quoted as "RA" everywhere (sqlite is case-insensitive but the spec keeps original spelling).
No NOT NULL constraints anywhere (notnull=0 on every column) despite PKs; sqlite PK on INTEGER is rowid alias so NULL insert becomes autoincrement — TS may silently get fresh ids.
Composite PKs: RA(student_id,prof_id), registration(course_id,student_id) — sample_fresh_primary_keys must dedupe on the tuple, not single column.
FK RA.student_id -> student.student_id and RA.prof_id -> prof.prof_id; registration.course_id -> course, registration.student_id -> student. All parents exist and are unique PKs.
RA.prof_id distinct=13 but prof has only 10 rows: FK values in original reference prof_ids 11..13 that do NOT exist in prof — dangling FK values in the original data (FK pragma off).
registration.student_id distinct=36 vs student 38 rows; RA.student_id distinct=21 — child FK sets are subsets, not full coverage.
grade has 5% NULLs (only nullable column in practice); TS String fuzzer drops None elements so it will never emit NULL for grade — a known TS miss.
gpa is REAL with 16 distinct values in [2.4,3.9]; Number fuzzer with scale=0 (no args) will draw integers in [-1,1] then perturb — implausible gpa values.

credit distinct=2 (2,3), diff distinct=5 (1..5), sat distinct=5 (1..5), popularity distinct=2, teachingability distinct=5, intelligence distinct=5, capability distinct=4 — tiny ENUM-like integer domains that Number fuzzer ignores.
salary is TEXT with values {med,high,low,free} — a categorical stored as text; String fuzzer will produce random charset strings, not these.
phone_number format '(NNN) NNNNNNN' and email format 'x@hku.hk'/'x@cuhk.edu.hk' — String fuzzer has no format awareness.
type in {RPG,TPG,UG}, gender in {Male,Female} — small enums; TS String fuzzer will not respect them.
operator_ts_expectations: All columns dispatch to Number (INTEGER/REAL) or String (TEXT); no Date/Time/Bool/Bit columns, so no date-template or bool quirks here.
Number fuzzer on INTEGER with no (a,b) args: scale=0, range [-1,1], int perturb +-1/+-2 — will produce values like -1,0,1,2,3, not the original 1..5 or 2..3 domains.
Number fuzzer on REAL gpa: scale=0, range [-1,1] floats, perturb +-0.01/+-0.02 — gpa values near 0, implausible (FN risk on gpa>3 style predicates).
String fuzzer on name/f_name/l_name/email/phone: random charset a-zA-Z 0-9() length 0..20 with 50% contaminate — no realistic names/emails/phones (FN on LIKE '%@hku%' etc.).

String fuzzer on enum-like TEXT (gender,type,salary,grade): random strings, so equality predicates on 'Male'/'UG'/'med'/'A' will mostly return empty — FP risk if gold also empty, FN if gold non-empty.
grade NULLs: String sampler drops None, so TS never produces NULL grade — queries with 'grade IS NULL' get empty result (FN).
Composite PK dedupe on (student_id,prof_id) and (course_id,student_id) will drop many rows; with small table sizes (level-0 = 1+30u, x4 per level) registration/RA may end up tiny.

FK fill draws from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement; RA.prof_id will only reference prof_ids that survived prof's PK dedupe (10 rows) — no dangling FKs in generated units (unlike original).
Table order: level 0 = {course, prof, student}, level 1 = {RA, registration}; sizes x4 per level so children larger than parents — plausible.
No unique single-column constraints besides PKs, so drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op here.
No CHECK constraints, no NOT NULL, no triggers/views — write_instance_sqlite will rarely skip rows (only PK collisions, already deduped).

Literal pool from train SQL will seed course.name, prof.first_name/last_name/email, student.f_name/l_name/email/phone, salary, grade, type, gender with real values — String sampler will mix these with random strings (p=0.2 fresh).
